simultaneously, the adversary selects a gain vector $g_t=(g_{1,t},\hdots,g_{K,t}) \in [0,1]^K$, possibly with the help of external randomization

symbols.psi_star: Legendre-Fenchel transform of the log-MGF bound psi

extra_assumptions: reward distributions satisfy the psi moment condition

source.label: th:ucb
source.quote: Assume that the reward distributions satisfy \eqref{eq:psicond}. Then $(\alpha, \psi)$-UCB with $\alpha > 2$ satisfies $$\oR_n \leq \sum_{i \,:\, \Delta_i > 0} \left( \frac{\alpha \Delta_i}{\psi^*(\Delta_i / 2)} \ln n + \frac{\alpha}{\alpha - 2}  \right)~.$$

results.notes: Survey; UCB due to Auer et al. 2002. Index uses ln t so anytime.

source.label: eq:regretUCBbounded
source.quote: In case of $[0,1]$-valued random variables, taking $\psi(\lambda) = \tfrac{\lambda^2}{8}$ ... gives the following pseudo-regret bound \oR_n \leq \sum_{i : \Delta_i > 0} \left( \frac{2 \alpha}{\Delta_i} \ln n + \frac{\alpha}{\alpha - 2}  \right)

results.notes: Corollary of Theorem 2.1 for alpha-UCB with Hoeffding.

bound.regime: liminf of R_n / log(T) as T -> infinity

extra_assumptions: strategy satisfies E T_i(n) = o(n^a) for all Bernoulli instances, suboptimal i, a>0

source.label: th:LR85
source.quote: Consider a strategy that satisfies $\E\,T_i(n) = o(n^a)$ for any set of Bernoulli reward distributions, any arm $i$ with $\Delta_i > 0$, and any $a>0$. Then, for any set of Bernoulli reward distributions the following holds $$\liminf_{n \to +\infty} \frac{\oR_n}{\ln n} \geq \sum_{i \,:\, \Delta_i > 0} \frac{\Delta_i}{\kl(\mu_i,\mu^*)}~.$$

results.notes: Extracted from Lai & Robbins 1985 (restricted to Bernoulli).

source.label: th:Exp3
source.quote: If Exp3 is run with $\eta_t=\eta = \sqrt{\frac{2 \ln K}{n K}}$, then \oR_n \leq \sqrt{2 n K \ln K}~.

results.notes: Losses in [0,1]; pseudo-regret holds against any adversary.

source.label: th:Exp3
source.quote: Moeover, if Exp3 is run with $\eta_t = \sqrt{\frac{\ln K}{t K}}$, then \oR_n \leq 2 \sqrt{n K \ln K}~.

results.notes: Anytime version.

extra_assumptions: delta given as input to the algorithm

source.label: th:exp3P
source.quote: For any given $\delta \in (0,1)$, if Exp3.P is run with $\beta = \sqrt{\frac{\ln(K \delta^{-1})}{n K}}, \eta = 0.95 \sqrt{\frac{\ln(K)}{n K}}, \gamma = 1.05 \sqrt{\frac{K \ln(K)}{n}}$ then, with probability at least $1-\delta$, R_n \leq 5.15 \sqrt{n K \ln(K \delta^{-1})}~.

results.notes: Gains in [0,1]; holds for non-oblivious adversary.

bound.regime: with probability at least 1-delta, any delta

source.label: th:exp3P
source.quote: Moreover, if Exp3.P is run with $\beta = \sqrt{\tfrac{\ln(K)}{n K}}$ while $\eta$ and $\gamma$ are chosen as before, then, with probability at least $1-\delta$, R_n \leq \sqrt{\frac{n K}{\ln(K)}} \ln(\delta^{-1}) + 5.15 \sqrt{n K \ln(K)}~.

results.notes: Algorithm does not need delta.

source.quote: If Exp3.P is run with $\beta = \sqrt{\frac{\ln K }{n K}}, \eta = 0.95 \sqrt{\frac{\ln K }{n K}}, \gamma = 1.05 \sqrt{\frac{K \ln K }{n}}$ then \E\,R_n \leq 5.15 \sqrt{n K \ln K} + \sqrt{\frac{n K}{\ln K }}~.

results.notes: Expected regret (not pseudo-regret), against non-oblivious adversary.

source.label: th:LBminimax
source.quote: Let $\sup$ be the supremum over all distribution of rewards such that, for $i=1,\dots,K$, the rewards $Y_{i,1},Y_{i,2},\ldots\in\{0,1\}$ are i.i.d., and let $\inf$ be the infimum over all forecasters. Then \inf \sup (...) \geq \frac{1}{20} \sqrt{n K}

results.notes: Explicit non-asymptotic inequality with constant 1/20; proved on stochastic Bernoulli instances, hence also a lower bound for adversarial. Attributed to Auer et al. 2002.

source.label: th:context-simple
source.quote: There exists a randomized forecaster for bandits with side information (the $\cS$-Exp3 forecaster, defined in the proof) that satisfies \oRS_n \le \sqrt{2n |\cS| K\ln K} for any set $\cS$ of contexts.

results.notes: Uses known-horizon Exp3 tuning per context; due to Maillard & Munos 2011.

source.label: th:Exp4
source.quote: Exp4 without mixing and with $\eta_t=\eta = \sqrt{\frac{2 \ln N}{n K}}$ satisfies \oRx_n \leq \sqrt{2 n N \ln K}~.

results.notes: Recorded as printed; the proof and surrounding text give sqrt(2 n K ln N), so the printed N and K are likely swapped (typo).

source.label: th:Exp4
source.quote: On the other hand, with $\eta_t = \sqrt{\frac{\ln N}{t K}}$ it satisfies \oRx_n \leq 2 \sqrt{n N \ln K}~.

results.notes: As printed; proof gives 2 sqrt(n K ln N), likely typo swap of N and K.

source.label: th:exp4-mixing
source.quote: Exp4 with mixing coefficient $\gamma$ and with $\eta_t = \eta = \gamma/K$ satisfies \oRx_n \le \frac{\gamma\,n}{2} + \frac{K\ln N}{\gamma}~.

results.notes: Bound holds for any gamma; horizon dependence only via tuning.

source.label: th:theta-regret
source.quote: There exists a randomized forecaster achieving \oR^{\Theta}_n = \mathcal{O}\left(n^{2/3}\left(\max_{\theta\in\Theta}|\cS_{\theta}|K\ln K\right)^{1/3}\sqrt{\ln|\Theta|}\right) for any class of context sets.

results.notes: Construction (Exp4 with mixing over S-Exp3 experts) given in proof; due to Maillard & Munos 2011.

bound.regime: T > d_vc; with probability at least 1-delta

symbols.d_vc: VC dimension of the policy class

extra_assumptions: K = 2 arms, binary policy class of VC dimension d

source.quote: For any class $\cF$ of binary policies $f : \cX\to\{0,1\}$ of VC-dimension $d$ and for all $n > d$, the forecaster VE run with $n' = \sqrt{n(2d\ln\frac{en}{d}+ \ln\frac{3}{\delta})}$ satisfies \sum_{t=1}^n \ell_{I_t,t} - n\inf_{f\in\cF}\ell_D(f) \leq c\sqrt{n(d\ln\frac{en}{d} + \ln\frac{3}{\delta})} for some constant $c > 0$ and with probability at least $1-\delta$

results.notes: Unspecified constant c, recorded with O notation. Regret vs n times risk of best policy (realized losses). From Beygelzimer et al. 2011.

bound.regime: T >= 8K; bound holds with infimum over U

symbols.L_U: cumulative multiclass hinge loss of comparator matrix U

source.quote:
If the Banditron algorithm is run with parameter $\gamma = (K/n)^{1/3}$ on any sequence $(x_1,y_1),\dots,(x_n,y_n)$ of examples such that $n \ge 8K$ and $
orm{x_t} = 1$, then the number $M_n$ of prediction mistakes satisfies \E\,M_n \le \inf_{U}( L_n(U) + (1 + 
orm{U}\sqrt{2 ar{L}_n(U)})K^{1/3}n^{2/3} + 2
orm{U}^2 K^{2/3}n^{1/3} + \sqrt{2}
orm{U} K^{1/6}n^{1/3})

results.notes: Bound on expected number of mistakes, not standard regret. Statement says labels in {-1,+1}, apparently a typo for {1,...,K}. From Kakade et al. 2008.

extra_assumptions: eta = sqrt(ln N/(3nd)), gamma = eta d

source.label: th:exp2john
source.quote: For any $\eta,\gamma > 0$ such that ${\eta d} \le {\gamma}$, Exp2 with John's exploration satisfies $\oR_n \leq 2 \gamma n + \frac{\ln N}{\eta} + \eta n d$. In particular, with $\eta = \sqrt{\frac{\ln N}{3 n d}}$ and $\gamma = \eta d$, $\oR_n \leq 2 \sqrt{3 n d \ln N}$.

results.notes: Paper's N = |action set| mapped to K. Extracted from Bubeck, Cesa-Bianchi, Kakade 2012.

source.label: th:osmdnegent
source.quote: For any set $\cC\subseteq\{0,1\}^d$, if OSMD is run on $\cK=\conv(\cC)$ with $F(x) = \sum_{i=1}^d x_i \ln x_i - \sum_{i=1}^d x_i$ ... In particular, with the estimate \eqref{eq:semibanditestimate} and $\eta= \sqrt{\frac{2m}{nd}\ln\frac{d}{m}}$, $\oR_n \leq  \sqrt{2 m d n \ln \frac{d}{m}}$.

results.notes: Paper notes projection may not be efficient in general. From Audibert, Bubeck, Lugosi 2011.

source.label: th:osmdzero
source.quote: In particular, choosing the $0$-potential $\psi(x) = (- x)^{-q}$, the estimate~\eqref{eq:semibanditestimate}, and $\eta= \sqrt{\frac{2}{q-1} \frac{m^{1 - 2/q}}{d^{1 - 2/q}}}$, $\oR_n \leq q \sqrt{\frac{2}{q-1} m d n}$.

results.notes: The stated eta seems to omit a 1/sqrt(n) factor; bound recorded as stated.

source.label: th:osmdzero
source.quote: With $q=2$ this gives $\oR_n \leq 2 \sqrt{2 m d n}$.

results.notes: For m=1 gives log-free sqrt(Kn) bound for adversarial MAB (INF).

source.label: th:two-point
source.quote: Let $\cK\subseteq\R^d$ be a closed convex set such that $r\,\Ball\subseteq\cK\subseteq R\,\Ball$ ... Then the following holds \oR_n \le \frac{R^2}{\eta} + \eta (Gd)^2 n + \delta\left(3 + \frac{R}{r} \right) G n~.

results.notes: G is the Lipschitz constant (L_lip).

symbols.R_rad: radius R with K inside R*Ball

source.label: th:two-point
source.quote: Moreover, if $\eta = \tfrac{R}{GD\sqrt{n}}$ then for $\delta\to 0$ we have that \oR_n \le 2RGd\sqrt{n}~.

results.notes: Limit as delta -> 0. Improved two-point rate from Agarwal, Dekel, Xiao 2010.
